answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, on-chain bond before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The protocol limits each bond’s influence and makes it slashable when identities coordinate to fake independent work, using auditable evidence and an appeal window. Creating a hundred accounts then requires a hundred funded deposits, not just a script; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it. A copper-backed bond may weather a glacier-long review, but each pulse of new identities still raises the cost.
